2026-09-03T12:40:27.2281856Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2282608Z 
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2283256Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2284198Z 
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2284918Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2285872Z 
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2288907Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2292544Z >
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2333498Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2338670Z >
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2340295Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2342022Z 
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2342397Z ### How to Use
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2342861Z 
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2344502Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2345894Z 
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2346243Z ```bash
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2348238Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2350319Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2355806Z ```
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2356757Z 
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2373710Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2374906Z ```bash
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2376005Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2378542Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2380950Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2383233Z ```
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2384511Z 
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2385797Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2388631Z ```bash
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2390930Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2410823Z ```
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2429180Z 
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2433379Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2446922Z ```bash
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2476441Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2478869Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2480309Z ```
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2480738Z 
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2481278Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2482328Z 
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2485177Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2490186Z 
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2490561Z ```bash
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2493056Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2495230Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2501581Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2502476Z 
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2514430Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2520055Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2522186Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2525080Z ```
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2525538Z 
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2527067Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2531394Z 
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2532001Z ```bash
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2533429Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2543356Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2546857Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2547777Z 
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2598859Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2606286Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2608378Z ```
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2608809Z 
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2609263Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2611525Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2614867Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2616780Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2621294Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2625331Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2626543Z 
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2626908Z ### Notes
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2628335Z 
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2629700Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2636414Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2735367Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2737936Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2740322Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2742938Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2744951Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-09-03T12:40:27.2746331Z </mcp-clis>
